: The mean and median on the dot plot for Table 2 data.
In the last example, the presence of the extremely low scores did not affect the median as much as the
mean. The median dropped from 82 to 80, still representing the typical values reasonably well, while the
mean became unreliable. This is generally true when there are extreme observations. We have already
noted that the mean is sensitive to extreme observations, and now we see that the median is
to extreme observations, meaning it is not greatly affected by extreme data
values. For this reason, the median is a better measure of center when there are extreme values in
The reason why the median is resistant to extreme observations is that it does not include each data value
in the computation. It only includes the order, or rank, of the data from smallest to largest, not the actual
values. Consider how the mean and median would be affected if the professor had input a typo on the
highest score as 195 instead of 95 as it was in
